# About me
::: {#about-content}

Hi! I’m Milena, a **quantitative social scientist**. I am looking to continue working in applied statistics, answering questions about how social contexts shape individual outcomes. My methodological interests include **measurement and psychometrics, multilevel and longitudinal modelling, Bayesian methods, and social network analysis.**

Through a bachelor’s in Psychology at Maastricht University, I learned to think about behaviour in context. I also found a passion for the quantitative side of research, especially the challenge of measuring things that aren’t directly observable, like well-being or trust. A master’s in Statistics and Data Science trained me in statistical modelling, measurement, and working with complex data. For my master's thesis at Statistics Netherlands (CBS), I worked with a whole-population network of the Netherlands to investigate how people's embeddedness within different social domains, such as work, neighbourhood, and household, relates to their willingness to trust others and strangers. I enjoy applying quantitative methods to answer relevant social questions, and questioning what the patterns I find actually mean in people’s daily lives.

I grew up in Brazil and moved to Belgium when I was eighteen, where I spent two years as an au pair, while learning Dutch at the KU Leuven. Watching children grow up in a different context than my own made me curious about how the environments we grow up in shape who we become. I am currently based in Leiden.

In my free time, you will find me taking care of my tropical plants, working in the garden, and having deep discussions about the meaning of life. I love learning about new cultures, reading about different perspectives, watching art house films, and going down rabbit holes about whatever has caught my attention lately. Whenever I get the chance, I also like to scuba dive.

:::
